data.title: Fetch Weather for the Chosen City

data.title: List and Filter Capitalized Files
data.description: Use the file system to list directory contents and filter for filenames that start with an uppercase letter.

data.title: Select a Rhyming City for Each File
data.description: For each filtered filename, apply a rhyming algorithm (or lookup table) to pick a city name that rhymes with the file name. If multiple matches exist, pick one at random.

data.title: Fetch Current Weather for the Chosen City
data.description: Call the weather service with the selected city name to retrieve the current weather conditions.

data.title: Compile and Deliver Results
data.description: Combine the filename, chosen city, and weather data into a concise report and output it (e.g., print to console or write to a log file).

data.title: Root Directory Discovery
data.description: Iterate through a predefined list of possible root paths (e.g., '/', '/home', '/var', 'C:\', etc.) and use `list_directory` to test each. The first path that returns a successful directory listing is selected as the root for the scan.

data.title: Recursive File Enumeration
data.description: Starting from the discovered root, repeatedly call `list_directory` to walk the directory tree depth‑first, collecting the full path of every regular file. Sub‑directories are queued for further listing until the entire tree is traversed.

data.title: Longest Path Calculation
data.description: Process the accumulated list of file paths, compute the character length of each full pathname, and keep the entry with the maximum length.

data.title: Result Notification
data.description: Emit the longest file path and its length to the user (e.g., via console output, email, or messaging service). If no files were found, report that outcome.

data.title: List Root Directory Contents
data.description: Use the list_directory tool to retrieve all items in the root directory without descending into subfolders.

data.title: Determine File Sizes
data.description: For each listed item, check if it is a file. If the list_directory output includes size metadata, use it directly; otherwise, read a small portion of the file with read_files_content1 to estimate its size and record the exact byte length.

data.title: Identify Largest File
data.description: Compare the recorded sizes and select the file with the maximum size.

data.title: Report Result
data.description: Return the name and size of the largest file to the user.

data.title: List Root Directory Contents
data.description: Retrieve the items in the root directory without recursion, then take the first 10 entries.

data.title: Filter Files and Gather Sizes
data.description: From the first 10 entries, keep only files. Use read_files_content1 (or metadata if available) to obtain each file's size in bytes.

data.title: Identify Largest File
data.description: Compare the sizes of the filtered files and select the one with the maximum size.

data.title: Report Result
data.description: Return the name and size of the largest file among the first 10 files to the user.

data.title: List Root Directory Contents
data.description: Retrieve a flat list of all files and directories directly under the root path.

data.title: Determine Longest Name
data.description: Iterate through the returned items, calculate the length of each name, and keep the item with the maximum length.

data.title: Report Result
data.description: Output the name (and optionally the type) of the longest‑named entry found at the root level.

data.title: List Root Directory Files
data.description: Retrieve a non-recursive list of all items in the root directory.

data.title: Identify Longest Filename
data.description: Parse the directory listing, filter out directories, and determine the file with the longest name.

data.title: Report Result
data.description: Output the name (and optional path) of the longest‑named file, handling cases where no files are found.

data.title: Trigger Automation
data.description: Start the workflow manually or on a scheduled interval (e.g., daily at 8 AM).

data.title: Select Five Random Cities
data.description: Pick five city names at random from a predefined master list (e.g., stored in a config file). If the list is empty, log an error and stop.

data.title: Fetch Current Weather for Selected Cities
data.description: Call the `get_multi_city_weather` service with the five chosen city names to retrieve temperature, conditions, and humidity for each.

data.title: Compile and Deliver Report
data.description: Format the weather data into a concise summary (e.g., bullet list) and output it to the console or send via email/notification. Include error handling for any failed city look‑ups.

data.title: Load Candidate Cities
data.description: Read a predefined file containing a list of city names to evaluate.

data.title: Fetch Current Weather for Cities
data.description: Query the weather service for all candidate cities to obtain their current temperatures.

data.title: Filter and Select Random City
data.description: From the returned data, keep only cities where temperature exceeds 50°F, then randomly pick one. If the filtered list is empty, mark the workflow as failed.

data.title: Report Result
data.description: Output the selected city and its temperature, or emit a failure message if no city met the criteria.
